articles.title: Teodoro pushes expanded Marine Corps presence in Kalayaan
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. is pushing for the accelerated development of the Philippine Marine Corps (PMC) and an expanded strategic presence in the Kalayaan Island…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. is pushing for the accelerated development of the Philippine Marine Corps (PMC) and an expanded strategic presence in the Kalayaan Island Group as the country strengthens its archipelagic defense capabilities.

Speaking at the PMC’s 76th anniversary celebration at Fort Bonifacio on Saturday, Teodoro said the Marines must expand their capabilities and establish strategic operating bases to strengthen their role in implementing the country’s Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept (CADC).

“As Major General [Bob] Apostol had said, the footprint of the Philippine Marine Corps of four marine brigades and one service support brigade for 7,600 islands is way, way too small,” Teodoro said, referring to the PMC commandant.

He stressed the need to maintain a credible presence and deterrence in the Kalayaan Island Group, requiring closer coordination among the Marines, Philippine Army, Philippine Navy, Philippine Air Force and Philippine Coast Guard.
The PMC is the naval infantry force under the Philippine Navy, tasked with conducting amphibious, expeditionary and special operations missions.

Teodoro called for a sustainable but urgent expansion plan for the Marines, including the establishment of strategic operating bases that could be co-located with other military facilities or built independently.
He also underscored the need to strengthen logistical readiness and maintain adequate physical reserves amid tightening global supply chains and increasing competition for resources.
“The notional reserves that we have are not sufficient. Physical custody and possession of reserves is the name of the game now,” he said.

Teodoro said the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), under President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., are working to accelerate defense modernization and readiness initiatives.

He also highlighted the importance of multilateral military exercises and stronger professional ties with foreign marine forces in identifying appropriate tactics, technologies and equipment suited to the country’s operational environment.

Beyond capability development, Teodoro called for greater investment in future military leaders through mentorship, cross-training, international engagement and early exposure to leadership responsibilities. /mcm

articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China
articles.summary:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority

The deportation of two more Uyghurs…

blocks.text: The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.
Now, two more men fear becoming the latest victims of Beijing’s repressive crackdown against the largely Muslim ethnic group, condemned by the UN as a potential crime against humanity.
The girlfriend of one of the men said her boyfriend, whose name is being withheld for security reasons, told the Guardian he wanted to go “anywhere else but China”.

Human rights groups said two Uyghur men were at risk of deportation after recently being transferred to an immigration detention centre and they feared Thai authorities may once again give in to pressure from Beijing.

Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, called for the men to be allowed to travel to a safe third country. “Previous Thai governments have kept Uyghurs in inhumane detention for years and then complied with Beijing’s demands to send them to China, where they were forcibly disappeared,” she said.

The men had been serving a seven-year prison sentence for offences related to an attempted escape from immigration detention in January 2020. They were part of a group of more than 200 Uyghur men, women and children who were apprehended by Thai police in 2014 near the border with Malaysia after they fled from China.

Since 2014, women and children in the group have been released to Turkey, while the men have been deported to China, in separate batches, attracting criticism from the United Nations and the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio.

blocks.caption: Uyghurs are taken away for questioning in 2014 in Thailand after crossing to south-east Asia through China’s southern border.   Photograph: The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images

blocks.text: Uyghurs, a Turkic minority mainly from the Xinjiang region in China, have been subjected to decades of oppressive and discriminatory treatment from the Chinese authorities. This has included the incarceration of hundreds of thousands of people in detention camps aimed at stamping out their cultural identity.
Beijing has defended its policies in Xinjiang as being aimed at poverty alleviation and counter-terrorism.

In July, Marzeyya Kasem’s (who asked to be referred to by her Islamic alias) boyfriend wrote to her in a letter that he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back to China. “Sometimes I thought why I’m a human being. What I do wrong against China … no want to go back to China,” he wrote. She shared the letter with a Thai rights group.
The two men facing imminent deportation reportedly pleaded their case to Thailand’s office of the National Human Rights Commission on Wednesday.
Relatives of Uyghurs have said the Chinese government was “paranoid about Uyghurs going to a safe country in large numbers and living together”, and preferred to have them deported.

It is not clear whether China has issued a formal extradition request for the two men. But Chaipruak Doungprapat, Thailand’s national security council chief, told reporters that the men, along with three other Uyghurs who are still in prison, had arrest warrants outstanding in China.

blocks.caption: A detention centre in China’s Xinjiang region, where treatment of the Uyghurs has been condemned by the UN as a potential crime against humanity. Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/AP

blocks.text: Some have questioned whether criminal warrants could be credible considering that at least one of them, Kasem’s boyfriend, was a minor when he left China. “If they are really wanted for a crime in China, why didn’t China immediately issue a [Interpol] red notice [when they were detained in 2014]?” asked Kasem.
Kasem believes that because Thailand was criticised for last year’s mass deportation, this time the authorities were trying to establish a more credible legal basis for the move.

A spokesperson for China’s foreign affairs ministry said: “The cooperation between China and Thailand in combating cross-border illegal and criminal activities such as smuggling is consistent with the laws of the two countries, international law and international practice.”
A spokesperson for Thailand’s foreign affairs ministry declined to comment.

items: Additional research by Rebecca Ratcliffe

articles.title: [Two Pronged] My husband’s porn consumption seems extreme
articles.summary: 'Is it normal — as my husband says and that I should just accept — that he watches pornography all the time?'

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr Holmes and Mr Baer,
I don’t know if you remember me, but five years ago, we had three video calls. I am Maria, from Turkey. I had a French partner and you helped me deal with him better.
I left my French boyfriend. I now have a husband. He is also French. I also need help with him.

Is it normal — as my husband says and that I should just accept — that he watches pornography all the time? He finishes work at lunchtime and when he comes home and I am cooking, he is watching porn. When he finishes his lunch and I am washing our dishes, he watches porn.

My husband leaves the house before 5 am so he is not late for his work. It starts before 6 am. This is why he is tired so right after lunch, he takes a nap. Before he takes a nap, he watches porn because he says it helps him relax. He even saves many of the pictures he sees. Many of these girls are nude, and some of them are so extreme, with their legs wide open, and their tongues always licking their lips or something that looks like a penis.
I do not like it. But if it is normal, I have to accept it. What should I do? Please help.
– Maria
Dear Maria,
Thank you for your message.

Now that almost anybody can access the internet, pornography is freely available, ubiquitous, and can be viewed anonymously. This has radically altered attitudes towards porn and in many circles it is no longer viewed as negatively as previously.

This is not to say that porn consumption is necessarily harmless. Although in some cases it can satisfy sexual curiosity, alleviate stress or boredom, combat loneliness, heavy usage can on the other hand influence sexual preferences, undermine trust and reduce intimacy in relationships, leading to feelings of inadequacy and even emotional abandonment.
Secrecy surrounding usage is also problematic, though this is not apparently an issue in your case, Maria.

It seems that your husband is quite open about his use of porn. He claims it helps him relax and sleep. Why he saves all those pictures however is perhaps less clear. The question then is: what is your objection to it?

For example, is it a matter of principle for you; do you believe all porn use is by definition bad? Is it that it has altered his sexual habits e.g. he wants to copy what he sees in videos? Is it perhaps that porn has reduced his ardor or increased his desire for novelty?
How has it affected your relationship? Has it changed his attitude towards you and if so, in what way? Has it reduced the intimacy between you? How else does it manifest?

Once you have a clearer idea of the answers to these and any related questions, then you will have a basic framework for another conversation with him about how his use of porn impacts both you individually and you as a couple.

This conversation should be non-judgmental and avoid blame, with each listening to the other’s point of view so as to understand and discern where future boundaries might be established. You might even consider counseling.

If this does not yield a compromise that you find comfortable and acceptable, you will need to weigh the pros and cons. Should he be unwilling to change significantly, are the negatives of his porn use something you can just live with? Alternatively, do they undermine your marriage to the extent that you want to take action?
An open and frank conversation aimed at improving mutual understanding and exploring options can hopefully bring greater intimacy and deepen your relationship.
Best wishes,
– JAF Baer
Thank you very much for your letter, and yes, I remember you with great fondness. I am glad you decided to write Two Pronged. This way, Mr Baer’s insights will also be included.

I agree with what he says about trying to understand what porn truly means to you. This would include not only your present — something totally unacceptable, his insisting you both try things he’s seen and insisting you try together things you do not want to? — but also your past — what you observed while growing up, what you were taught, etc.

I feel how I can help you most is to encourage what Mr Baer suggested, which is to explore more deeply “how (his porn watching) affected your relationship? And also “has it reduced the intimacy between you?”

At present, your relationship is unequal; where your husband (let’s call him Nathan) gets to say what normal is, with your having to accept it as normal and therefore, acceptable, because of nothing more than his opinion.
Your writing to Two Pronged shows a step in the right direction: wanting an outside resource to verify your “suspicions” vis-à-vis Nathan’s pronouncement that porn is normal.

For the avoidance of doubt it need not be Two Pronged per se that makes it the correct step, but any other resource that is both evidence-based and clearly distinguishes between science and mere opinion.
Perhaps, a realistically accessible guide for any person to gauge their partner’s “normality” would be the 5-D’s framework professors in Abnormal Psychology share with their undergrad students.
These include:

items: Deviance: Is Nathan’s porn watching significantly different from societal, cultural, or statistical norms? Not that being deviant is enough to label something as inherently a disorder. For example, possessing not just Patis Tesoro’s unsurpassed creativity but the grit and hard work to make such designs a reality is “deviant” (but not a disorder). That is the reason she is a national artist and we are not. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case.

Danger: Behaviors that pose a risk of harm to either Nathan or to others (like yourself) e.g. suicide ideation, aggressive violence etc. which would require immediate attention. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case (at the moment).
Dysfunction: resulting in a person’s inability to handle daily life e.g. working or maintaining relationships. This is a relevant issue in your case, as it is affecting the quality of your marriage.

Distress: The emotional pain, suffering, or anguish the behavior or condition causes the individual. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case, because the distress mentioned here refers only to Nathan. One might even comment that distress seems the very opposite of what Nathan feels when he watches porn.

Duration: How long the symptoms or behaviors have lasted. Temporary emotional reactions to a stressful life event are normal, whereas porn watching that persists continuously over an extended period points toward a clinical disorder. This does NOT seem a relevant issue here since this only focuses on how long your husband has been watching porn, not you.

blocks.text: If you can move beyond asking a credible resource what normal is, and have the confidence to ask yourself what you would consider normal in a marriage, then that would be a bigger/better step towards achieving even better mental health!
That saying, “What is normal for the spider is chaos for the fly,” fits your situation perfectly!

You do not have to have an evidence-based, ultra logical reason for not wanting to experience your Nathan’s constant porn watching. Everyone in your barkada (friend group) may think it ok, but the fact that you do not, that it causes you distress, is enough reason to talk about it with Nathan and find a solution acceptable to both of you.

In my clinical experience, a marriage where both partners feel safe because they feel loved is a relationship that does not insist on outside experts to convince the other an issue is worth focusing on.

If it distresses one’s partner, that alone is sufficient reason to try and find solutions that work for you both. All you need to say is “This makes me sad/angry/feel humiliated, please stop” to the partner. Because he loves and respects his wife, he will at the very least try. Nathan is definitely not at that stage yet.

How long you want to wait until he does…IF he does…depends entirely on you. That decision can be difficult. Please remember, dearest Maria, that we are right here to help you make it should you want us to.
Wishing you the clarity and courage to decide what is best for you.
– MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

articles.title: One Pinoy dead in Persian Gulf tanker explosion
articles.summary: The DMW said that the incident occurred aboard the MT Velos Sapphire, a Marshall Islands-flagged vessel, while it was en route to Sitrah, Bahrain.

blocks.text: November 8, 2026 | 10:56am
Photo showing MT Velos Sapphire
Department of Migrant Workers via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — One Filipino seafarer has died after an explosion aboard an oil products tanker in the Persian Gulf in the early morning hours of November 5, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said.
In a statement on Saturday, November 7, the DMW said that the incident occurred aboard the MT Velos Sapphire, a Marshall Islands-flagged vessel, while it was en route to Sitrah, Bahrain.

While initial reports suggest a drone attack may have caused the blast, authorities noted that the exact cause of the explosion remains unverified. The DMW said no environmental damage or oil spillage has been reported following the blast.
Meanwhile, 21 other Filipino crew members were reported safe and unharmed
The vessel's licensed manning agency has notified the bereaved family after receiving official confirmation from the shipowner, and is currently providing guidance and assistance.
The shipowner has also extended its condolences and pledged full support to the victim's relatives, according to the DMW.
Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said that the government is taking immediate steps to assist the family.
“We will provide all the support and guidance the bereaved family needs during this difficult time," Cacdac said.

The DMW confirmed it is also maintaining close coordination with both the shipowner and relevant international authorities to track ongoing developments, investigate the circumstances behind the blast, and ensure all necessary aid reaches the victim's family.

articles.title: Cold blast brings springtime snow to alpine regions as temperatures plummet across Australia’s south-east
articles.summary:
Thredbo, Perisher and Mount Hotham all recorded falls, along with kunanyi/Mount Wellington in Tasmania

  • Get our

blocks.text: Snow has fallen across parts of NSW, Victoria and Tasmania as an unseasonal cold blast whips through Australia’s south-east.
Thredbo, Perisher and Mount Hotham all recorded falls, while snow also fell on Kunanyi/Mount Wellington in Hobart.

The snow had been forecast by the Bureau of Meteorology (BoM), and though uncommon, it is not entirely unusual – many of the places hit by snow in the past 24 hours also recorded a fall in November 2022.
The falls brought a rush of posts on social media from those puzzled by the unseasonal spring weather.

blocks.caption: The Perisher Valley snow stake at 8:18am, on Sunday 8 November 2026. Photograph: Perisher Valley

blocks.text: “You will not believe this, it’s springtime in Australia, in November, and it’s snowing,” Madeleine McVie, a retail manager at Thredbo, posted on Instagram on Saturday afternoon.
“Like, not just a little bit. It’s fully snowing.”
McVie posted another clip on Sunday morning of her riding empty chairlifts through the park as the snow continued to fall.
Kingston Crows cricket club in Tasmania posted an image of the Kingston Beach Oval on Saturday that showed it coated in hailstones.
after newsletter promotion

The BoM said a weather system, filled with cold air moving north from towards Antarctica, had caused the wintery chill with apparent temperatures much cooler than forecast maximums. South-westerly winds were also causing the apparent or “feels like” temperature to be lower.
At midday, Adelaide, Melbourne, Hobart, Canberra and Sydney all had temperatures that felt cooler than 13 degrees.
The highest temperature at that time was in Adelaide, with a top of 17.5C that felt like 12.3C, with Canberra the lowest (a maximum of 12.9C that felt like 5.3C).
Brisbane, Perth and Darwin, meanwhile, were all enjoying temperatures in the 20s or 30s.
Warmer temperatures are forecast for Monday, and all capital cities are expected to reach at least 20C by Tuesday.
It may be one of the last cold snaps of the year – the BoM, as well as the UN and other bodies, have warned about the likely impacts of a “jaw dropping” supercharged El Niño.

blocks.caption: Vehicles are submerged and damaged on a flooded street following heavy rainfall in Erbil, Ira. Severe downpours caused widespread flooding across the city, leaving cars trapped in rising waters, on November 7, 2026. Photograph: Ahsan Mohammed Ahmed Ahmed/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: The climate crisis, caused by pollution from fossil fuels, is already supercharging extreme weather and killing people. The El Niño is expected to ratchet up the effects even further, and has already begun to affect regions across the planet as weather patterns are altered.
The southern hemisphere summer is predicted to be hotter and drier as a result of the huge El Niño, meaning greater wildfire risk and droughts in Australia and southern Africa.

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte defense opposes prosecution's bid to submit expert report to ICC
articles.summary: The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has opposed the prosecution's bid to submit an expert report as evidence in his crimes against humanity of murder case before the International…

blocks.text: November 8, 2026 | 10:34am

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has opposed the prosecution's bid to submit an expert report as evidence in his crimes against humanity of murder case before the International Criminal Court (ICC), questioning its late submission and the inclusion of related materials.

In an 8-page request originally filed on October 30 and released on November 6, defense lawyer Peter Haynes asked ICC Trial Chamber III to dismiss the prosecution's fourth application under Rule 68(3), arguing that it failed to seek permission to include the expert report and its associated materials in its list of evidence.
The report, prepared by prosecution witness P-1400, was received by the prosecution after the deadline for submitting its list of evidence, according to the defense.

On October 23, prosecutors informed Trial Chamber III that P-1400, whose field of expertise remains undisclosed, had provided an expert report covering redacted topics relevant to Duterte's case. They also sought to introduce 15 associated items alongside the report under Rule 68(3).
Haynes said the prosecution had not explained why it did not seek leave to submit the report earlier, despite having received it weeks after the deadline.
The defense argued that the timing could affect Duterte's ability to prepare his case.

"This omission affects Mr Duterte's ability to prepare his defence, particularly as P-1400 is expected to be the [REDACTED] witness called by the Prosecution and the associated materials are extensive," the filing read.

The defense did not generally oppose the use of expert reports under Rule 68(3). However, it questioned the inclusion of two other studies cited in P-1400's report, saying the witness did not sufficiently discuss or explain their contents.

"In reality, the Prosecution is attempting indirectly to introduce material prepared by other professionals who are not on its witness list via the instant Expert Report which - by its own admission - only '[REDACTED]'," the filing read.
"These additional materials do not form an integral part of P-1400's evidence," it added.
Haynes also objected to documents they considered repetitive and of little relevance to the proceedings.
"Their introduction would be redundant, and would burden the Chamber with evidence of negligible relevance, contrary to its express directions," the filing read.

The defense asked the chamber to dismiss the prosecution's application or defer its consideration until the judges decide on the request to add the documents to the list of evidence. It also asked the chamber to reject the proposed redacted materials as associated evidence under Rule 68(3).
Prosecutors submit updated witness list
In a separate filing dated November 6, the ICC Office of the Prosecutor submitted an updated list of witnesses following an order from Trial Chamber III.
The prosecution identified witnesses who may testify through audio-video link (AVL) technology and updated their anticipated order of appearance.
The chamber had directed the prosecution to provide the number of witnesses expected to testify remotely, their anticipated calling order and any foreseeable issues with AVL testimony.
The prosecution said it would inform the chamber, the parties and participants if circumstances would allow the witnesses to testify in person.
"The Prosecution does not currently foresee any issues with respect to AVL testimony," the filing read.

The updated witness list was attached as a confidential annex because it contains sensitive witness information. The public filing did not disclose the names or number of witnesses included in the list.
The submission was signed by Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.
Duterte's trial set to open Nov. 30
Duterte's trial before the ICC is scheduled to open on November 30 at 10 a.m. in The Hague, Netherlands.

The judges will first verify whether Duterte understands the charges against him and ask him to enter a plea. The prosecution and the legal representatives of victims will then deliver their opening statements, followed by the defense if it chooses to make one.

The prosecution has been given six hours to present its opening statement, while the victims' representatives have three hours. The first prosecution witness is expected to testify after the opening statements.

The ICC confirmed all charges of crimes against humanity against Duterte on April 23, 2026, and committed him to trial. He faces three counts involving alleged murders and attempted murders linked to the war on drugs.

articles.title: Elks to face Alouettes in Grey Cup after beating Lions in West final
articles.summary: Cody Fajardo used his legs and his arms to engineer two fourth-quarter touchdowns to guide the Edmonton Elks to a 28-16 win over the B.C. Lions in the West Division final on Saturday.

image.caption: Elks quarterback Cody Fajardo throws a pass under pressure from Lions linebacker Darnell Sankey during the CFL West final on Saturday in Edmonton. (Codie McLachlan/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: CFL·Breaking
Cody Fajardo used his legs and his arms to engineer two fourth-quarter touchdowns to guide the Edmonton Elks to a 28-16 win over the B.C. Lions in the West Division final on Saturday.
113th Grey Cup goes Nov. 15 at McMahon Stadium in Calgary
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Nov 07, 2026 9:29 PM EST | Last Updated: 30 minutes ago

With 40,183 noisy fans at Edmonton's Commonwealth Stadium — the CFL's largest crowd of the year — two key Fajardo second-down runs of 11 and 14 yards ended with rough play penalties against B.C. The Elks capitalized both times with Fajardo scoring on a five-yard run and later hitting Austin Mack with a 23-yard touchdown strike for a 25-16 margin.

Justin McInnis fumbled after a pass reception and Edmonton's JJ Ross returned it to the B.C. 20. Three plays later Vincent Blanchard's third field goal of the night gave Edmonton a 28-16 lead with three minutes left.
The Elks will meet the Montreal Alouettes in the Grey Cup in Calgary next Sunday. Montreal earned its spot earlier Saturday with a hard-fought 33-23 win over the Winnipeg Blue Bombers.

items: Montreal Alouettes defeat Winnipeg Blue Bombers in CFL East final

blocks.text: The first time either team started a drive in the opponent's side of midfield came midway through the third quarter. Montrell Washington returned a punt 35 yards to the B.C. 54 but two straight penalties promptly moved the Elks back to their own 49. Fajardo then ran for 15 yards and a rough play penalty put the Elks on the B.C. 18-yard line. A 13-yard pass to Mack set up Fajardo's run for the game's first major and a 16-9 lead.

The Lions instantly responded. Four straight successful passes, including a 33-yarder to James Butler, left the lions second and two on the Edmonton eight. Quarterback Nathan Rourke broke loose over the left side and pushed his way into the end zone 37 seconds into the fourth quarter.
Another Fajardo run, this one for 15 yards, and a second rough play penalty set up Blanchard's 46-yard field to put Edmonton back ahead 19-16 at 3:15.
Both offences struggled through the first 30 minutes that ended with B.C. up 9-6 on the strength of three Sean Whyte field goals. Blanchard kicked a pair of field goals for Edmonton.

The Elks opened the game with a 10-play, 42-yard drive that ended with Blanchard's first field goal, from 21 yards. A 48-yard boot by Blanchard at 11:36 made it 6-0 but Edmonton's next four possessions ended with punts.

The Lions got three second-quarter field goals from Whyte of 13, 29 and 42 yards. The visitors had only one sustained drive, seven plays for 52 yards. But Rourke began to find some cracks in Edmonton's No. 1 ranked defence with lengthy passes to set up Whyte's kicks.

articles.title: Gifting with a purpose: Filipino brands doing more than just selling
articles.summary: These small businesses give back to the communities they serve

blocks.text: Every holiday season, we remember that the most important thing about gifts is making our recipients feel seen and special. There’s nothing quite like watching joy bloom on someone’s face as you hand them something they’ve always wanted or that makes their life easier. There’s also nothing quite like using your gift to support others along the way. What if your gift could help the sick, or stop rivers from being clogged? What if your gift could give back to a community in need?

Standing for “Alternative Nest and Trading/Training Hub for Indigenous or Ingenious Little Livelihood seekers”, true to their name, they help our indigenous groups have a space and name in the market. This is the place if you’re looking to gift stylish woven apparel, accessories, home decor, or even whole fabric by the meter, along with custom orders and alterations. Moreover, Anthill has sustainable zero-waste programs: bringing life back into scrap fabric via their reweave project, accepting unwanted fabric in their circulatory hub, and offering lifetime repairs and consults. So in a world of fast fashion, rest assured any gift you buy from them will reduce fabric waste and last long-term.
Get them here:
https://anthillmarkets.com/ https://anthillfabrics.com/

For over a decade, LoveHopeFaith Group has been helping people fight the Big C— cancer— with charities and donations. Their Lifesaver watches are not only affordable, classic, and stylish, but 50% of their proceeds go to their sponsored cancer patients.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Brave Story (@thebravestory)

As cheesy as it sounds, art brings us together. And we wouldn’t have art without the people behind it who trained their craft to show their hearts. Kâtha is one such place that supports local artists. If you’re looking for everything about art, from illustration to artisanal works and fashion, you can find it at Kâtha, and it goes beyond putting their work on the market: Kâtha also does training, workshops, advocacy campaigns, and brings their artists’ voices to policy reworks.
Visit their instagram page here.

Cara Welfare is an animal welfare organization that cares for stray cats and dogs. While we don’t recommend gifting pets, we definitely recommend sponsoring care for a furry friend or two in the giftee’s name. And hey, in the future, your giftee can foster on their own terms, or adopt them into a fur-ever home.
Visit their website here.

The water hyacinth is a non-endangered aquatic plant notable for its rapid reproduction… and the invasive effects of its proliferation on the ecosystem and living communities. To help keep its population in check, Jacinto and Lirio source their plant-based leather from the water hyacinth and turn it into a variety of leatherworks, like accessories, bags, and stationery. They also provide custom orders.

A shameless plug. There’s no shame in supporting the press, so why not gift a subscription to independent investigative journalism? It also comes with audio articles, exclusive articles, and, depending on your plan, discounts on other Rappler media and exclusive events. You can also gift one-time donations in your giftee’s name.
Whichever gift you choose from this list, you’ll know it’s a gift that gives back in the Filipino spirit. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Czarina Yasmin Sia. Czarina is an earnest creator whose works focuses on the little things and helping others. She enjoys engaging with unconventional ways to tells stories and is eager to write about life’s overlooked aspects. A graduating Communication Arts student from De La Salle University Manila, she aims to inspire people to find wonder.

articles.title: Meet Elias Gish, the FEU rookie turning heads in UAAP basketball
articles.summary: Elias Gish, a 6-foot-7 teenager from the Gilas Pilipinas Youth program, steadily stakes his claim for a future takeover of the contending FEU Tamaraws with his no-nonsense, defense-oriented play

blocks.text: THE FUTURE. Rookie Elias Gish proves to be a potential star for the FEU Tamaraws
UAAP
Elias Gish, a 6-foot-7 teenager from the Gilas Pilipinas Youth program, steadily stakes his claim for a future takeover of the contending FEU Tamaraws with his no-nonsense, defense-oriented play

items: The FEU Tamaraws are strong contenders in the UAAP Season 89 men's basketball tournament, with several key players contributing to their success.
Elias Gish, an 18-year-old player, showed potential in a recent game against UE, scoring 13 points and earning praise from coach Sean Chambers.
Despite limited playing time and muted averages, Gish is part of a championship-contending rotation, indicating a promising future for him in the league.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Across 10 games in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament, the FEU Tamaraws have emerged as one of the upper-tier contenders in an ultra-competitive field still boasting seven possible Final Four candidates.

Much credit can go around when pinpointing the architects of this current surge from the men in Morayta, like coach Sean Chambers, star big man Mo Konateh, do-it-all forward Kirby Mongcopa, veteran sniper Jorick Bautista, and even struggling MVP Janrey Pasaol.
Elias Gish may not be a name that gets lumped together with the previous ones just yet, but signs are starting to show that his time in the spotlight may come sooner than later.

Last Wednesday, November 4, in a game against the hapless UE Red Warriors that became a tale of two halves, the 18-year-old project from California earned himself an extended leash, and certainly made the most of it.
In 22 minutes off the bench, the 6-foot-7 Gish tallied 13 points — including 8 points in the second half that saw FEU pull away from a threatening UE upset bid — on top of 6 rebounds and 3 blocks.

While playing against a Red Warriors squad with an ongoing 30-game losing streak is not exactly the best measuring stick of talent, the fact remains that Gish is a kid in a land of young men, and that he still earned respect from a legend like Chambers after his breakout showcase.

“[Gish] just turned 18 back in January and technically, a lot of kids here play in the 19-and-under division, but he’s such a phenomenal talent,” said the former PBA Best Import and six-time PBA champion.
“Today, I thought he was ready. He needs to get more responsibilities, and we saw that what he can do on the basketball court is phenomenal,” Chambers added of the oversized Gilas Youth guard.

Though Gish is nowhere near the Rookie of the Year race with muted averages of 4.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, 0.8 steals, and 0.6 blocks in just a little over 14 minutes per game, he is still a consistent part of a championship-contending rotation, which says a lot of what is yet in store.

“I’m just playing my role, honestly. Whatever coach tells me to do, that’s my role, and I executed it today. I just got to be consistent every game and just keep getting reps in and working hard on the court,” Gish said.
“For me, obviously, it’s just been about adapting to everything here. Especially the system and league in general, it’s something I’m not used to compared to back in the States.”

The potential also shone through with the national team, as Gish recently averaged 5.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.7 steals, and 0.7 blocks in just 19 minutes per game in the FIBA U18 Asia Cup.

While it may take some more time for the Fil-Am prospect to get more playing time, especially as FEU jostles for Final Four position in the season’s home stretch, Gish’s complete rise now seems like a matter of when, not if, and fans should definitely stay tuned when that time comes.

Yet again, FEU continues to prove why it is truly a hotbed of rising Filipino talent with their acquisition of Gish, and why the 20-time champion Tamaraws are still the most successful program in UAAP men’s basketball history. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Trash to treasure: Made Here turns waste into art at Ibagiw 2026
articles.summary: From sachet mosaics to furniture made from salvaged materials, Baguio artists give waste a second life while making creativity pay

blocks.text: UPCYCLING. Discarded glass bottles find new purpose as hanging lamps by Made Here Artesanos, illuminating Rochelle Bakisan’s 'Ang Plastic Naten!,' a mosaic of Baguio City made from discarded sachet wrappers.
Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler
From sachet mosaics to furniture made from salvaged materials, Baguio artists give waste a second life while making creativity pay

items: The Made Here exhibit in Baguio City transforms discarded materials into functional art, aligning with the theme of RIKUS: A Creative Circular Baguio.
Artists Dulthe Carlo Munar and Rochelle Bakisan showcase innovative pieces, including a mosaic made from sachet wrappers that highlights environmental issues related to plastic waste.
The initiative aims to promote circularity by creating opportunities for artists to sell their work, encouraging sustainability through the repurposing of materials into useful household items.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — What do discarded sachets, old horseshoes, empty bottles, and scrap metal have in common?
In the hands of Baguio’s creative minds, they become art. Better yet, art you can actually use.

At the basement of the Baguio Cultural and Convention Center, the Made Here exhibit is putting an inventive spin on Ibagiw 2026’s theme, RIKUS: A Creative Circular Baguio, by turning materials destined for disposal into artworks, furniture, and functional household pieces.

The exhibit brings together architect and artist Dulthe Carlo Munar, mixed media artist Rochelle Bakisan, and Made Here Artesanos, the in-house creative team behind the initiative of Wright Park Hotel.

blocks.caption: A wooden cart-inspired lamp and other handcrafted pieces show architect and artist Dulthe Carlo Munar’s playful approach to design, combining craftsmanship, imagination, and everyday functionality. All photos by Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler

blocks.text: For hotel general manager Ompong Palma, joining Ibagiw was a natural next step.

“We were already doing it,” Palma said, referring to the hotel’s circularity initiative that began in June. When the invitation came, the team decided to expand the concept and bring the Made Here experience to the festival.
Among the exhibit’s eye-catching pieces is Bakisan’s Ang Plastic Naten!, a six-foot by eight-foot mosaic assembled entirely from discarded sachet wrappers.
The artwork recreates familiar Baguio landmarks, including the Baguio Cathedral, surrounded by colorful flowers and greenery.
But there is a catch to its beauty. The materials that make the cityscape possible are also part of the environmental problem it addresses.
The artwork encourages viewers to refuse unnecessary single-use plastics rather than simply finding new uses for them.

blocks.caption: Repurposed wooden barrels become the base of a glass-topped table by Made Here Artesanos, surrounded by lighting fixtures and decorative pieces fashioned from discarded materials. Among the displayed works are fish sculptures made with electronic circuit boards, showing how even obsolete technolo…

blocks.text: Born and raised in Baguio, Bakisan draws inspiration from Cordillera culture while experimenting with unconventional materials, including coffee, soil, and natural pigments.
She also conducts art workshops, advocates environmental causes, and transforms used denim and clothing into bags and crafts through her small business, Boslay Arts and Crafts.
Her message is that art does not always require expensive materials. Sometimes, it begins with what people already have.
Munar brings a different kind of ingenuity to the exhibit.
A registered architect and longtime artist, he combines wood, metal, and mechanical elements to create pieces that blur the boundaries between sculpture, design, and engineering.

Munar began exhibiting his work in 1980 while pursuing an academic career. After retiring from teaching in 2022, he devoted himself to art full-time, exploring movable wooden sculptures and other experimental forms.
His creative approach fits comfortably alongside the functional pieces produced by Made Here Artesanos.

Throughout the exhibit, discarded materials find unexpected purposes. Horseshoes become wall hooks, bottles form illuminated furniture, and salvaged wood and metal are turned into lamps and other household objects.
Some pieces look industrial, others playful. All invite visitors to reconsider what deserves to be thrown away.
Palma believes upcycling should go beyond producing beautiful objects.
“What we’re looking for is functionality,” he explained.
He wants the initiative to create opportunities for artists and craftspeople whose products can find buyers, generate income, and sustain their creative work.
“When we say circularity, it’s a circle,” Palma said, emphasizing that repurposing materials should give them a genuinely useful new life.

blocks.caption: Wright Park Hotel general manager Ompong Palma (left) and retail manager Christian Eric Coronacion (right), both part of Made Here Artesanos, at the Ibagiw 2026 exhibit, which promotes functional upcycling.

blocks.text: The team is also inviting other artists working with discarded materials to present their ideas and explore possible collaborations.
And unlike exhibits where visitors can only admire the displays, the pieces at Made Here are available for purchase.

It is an interesting proposition for Baguio’s creative economy. A discarded object becomes a product, an artist earns from the work, and a buyer takes home something with both purpose and personality.
After all, sustainability is easier to appreciate when it comes with good design and something useful for the house.

Made Here is open until November 26 at the basement of the Baguio Cultural and Convention Center, giving Ibagiw visitors an opportunity to meet the makers, explore their creations, and perhaps take home something that has already lived one life and is ready for another. – Rappler.com

articles.title: UFC boss Dana White says he's meeting with Trump after press secretary job offer
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump and UFC president and CEO Dana White are seen at the White House on June 14. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.
U.S. president has attended several UFC events with close friend White

Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson.

White, who was in London on Saturday for a boxing event, was asked at a news conference about Trump's post and responded by saying that he planned to fly to Washington right after and meet with Trump on Monday.
When asked how he would balance the job with the current positions he has in the fighting world, White seemed confused by the question and then said, "Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already."
He declined to say what conversations he'd had with Trump but said, "I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that."

items: How the UFC became a stage for Trump

blocks.text: Before the news conference, the UFC head shared an image of Trump's post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words "On to the next chapter."
The White House and a spokesperson for the UFC did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.

Trump said in his post that he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as "assistants," adding, "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"

While White didn't make it clear if he was seriously considering the position of becoming the primary spokesperson for the president of the United States, he did elsewhere in his news conference describe his ambitions to expand the Zuffa Boxing organization he also runs with Saudi Arabian backers and hold more of its events around the world.
Transition period

Trump's post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president's impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump's inner circle.

items: Trump names Stephen Miller as new chief of staff after midterm drubbing

blocks.text: The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance with reporters before leaving the job after five days.
The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.
Close friends
Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.

He brought White and the sport to the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of its independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under "the Claw," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

items: Trump gets ringside seat at White House UFC event on his 80th birthday

blocks.text: "It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one," said White afterward.
White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne to remain in public hands after partial backtrack on defence property selloff
articles.summary:
Four heritage-listed defence properties to be preserved for community use after backlash from veterans and former PMs

  • Get our

blocks.text: Four heritage-listed defence sites, including Sydney’s Victoria Barracks, will remain in public hands after the Albanese government yielded to public backlash against their sale.

The sites, along with 63 others around the country, were identified in an independent audit as being underutilised by defence, not fit for purpose and costly to maintain, and were earmarked for sale to recoup $3bn in the federal budget.

But the plan to sell off the heritage-listed sites drew fierce opposition from public campaign group Save Victoria Barracks Sydney, veterans and high-profile politicians including former prime ministers John Howard and Paul Keating.

Ahead of an important cabinet meeting on the budget on Monday, the Albanese government confirmed on Sunday that four sites – Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne, and Fort Queenscliff and RAAF Base Point Cook in Victoria – will remain publicly owned and their historic elements preserved for community use after they are vacated by defence personnel.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said Victoria Barracks Sydney held a “special place in our nation’s history” while the defence minister, Richard Marles, said the military needed to focus its spending on keeping people safe.
“Given the strategic landscape we face, we cannot afford to be wasting money. We need to look at how we best use defence money for defence capability,” Marles said.
“By moving personnel off these sites, and working to open them up for the public we are ensuring that the history of Victoria Barracks is one that can be protected and returned to all Australians.”
The government will work with the Australian War Memorial once the sites are free to transform the sites into public spaces that tell the history of Australia’s military.
Sydney’s Victoria Barracks was built between 1840 and 1848 and was originally occupied by the British army. It is also the site of the city’s oldest wine cellar.
The shadow defence minister, James Paterson, said questions remain about whether the military should have a presence and capability in Melbourne and Sydney.

“While this is a win for Australia’s defence heritage, it is only the beginning. The Coalition will continue to fight to save other critical defence sites, including HMAS Penguin, Lancer Barracks, Irwin Barracks, and more,” he said.
The NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, said the site was an “irreplaceable part of our military heritage that deserves to be protected for future generations”.
“Our military heritage and defence capability must come before a short-term cash grab,” she said.
The multi-year audit, completed in 2023, was tasked with identifying surplus and costly property holdings, often costing millions to maintain.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Victoria Barracks in Melbourne. The sales of the Sydney and Melbourne Victoria Barracks had been expected to raise $1.3bn, given their prime locations in the biggest capital cities. Photograph: Michael Currie/AAP

blocks.text: The audit found underutilised sites are “draining resources from higher priority needs” for defence.

“Today’s estate footprint comprises numerous legacy sites without a clear ongoing link to current or future capabilities. Urgent interventions are needed to correct the unsustainable trajectory that has resulted from decades of deferred decisions on contentious estate issues,” it said.
The sales of the Sydney and Melbourne Victoria Barracks were expected to raise $1.3bn, given their prime locations in the biggest capital cities.

Up to $2.4bn was expected to be raised from the sale of 26 major metropolitan sites, saving about $3bn in upkeep and security costs over 10 years. These include sites in Randwick, Sydney; Sandringham and St Kilda in Melbourne; Petrie Terrace in Brisbane; and Fremantle in Western Australia.
The government hopes the sales will free up land for new housing developments with a long-term target of 6,000 new dwellings.
Defence expects personnel will have vacated six sites by the end of the year.

The announcement comes as cabinet’s expenditure review committee, which determines budget decisions, meets on Monday after the official interest rate was lifted to an 18-year high of 4.85% in a bid to combat persistent inflation this week.
The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, said this week higher fuel prices due to the Middle East conflict were the “primary driver” of inflation rather than the government’s budget.

There will be also security deployment outside of Metro Manila as the country gears up to welcome global leaders for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits on November 16 to 18, the organizing council said on Sunday.
Retired Major General Potenciano Camba, ASEAN National Organizing Council deputy director general for operations, said some guests could arrive in Clark, Pampanga and Subic, Zambales.

"We have a very significant security deployment all over Metro Manila and outside Metro Manila. Sa paghahanda natin, ang main arrival natin ay Manila, pero may mga alternate tayo na arrival area lalo na ang Clark at Subic," he told Super Radyo dzBB.

(We have a very significant security deployment all over Metro Manila and outside Metro Manila. In our preparation, our main arrival point is Manila, but we have alternate arrival areas, especially Clark and Subic.)
Moreover, the organizing council said that it has monitored possible protests during the summit.
"May mga impormasyon tayo na, alam mo naman demokrasya ang ating bansa, may mga report ng protesta. Pero sa panuntunan ng PNP, kaya naman nilang i-address," said Camba.
(We have information that—you know our country is a democracy—there are reports of protests. But under the guidelines of the PNP, they are capable of addressing them.)
As part of security measures, there will be exclusion zones at the Philippine International Convention Center — the venue for the international event — where entry is subject to screening.
"Doon sa Philippine International Convention Center sa Pasay, magkakaroon tayo ng exclusion zone. So magiging restricted ang vehicle entry at mga hindi authorized na hindi papasok doon," said Camba.

(There at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay, we will have an exclusion zone. So vehicle entry will be restricted, and unauthorized individuals will not be allowed to enter there.)
The Philippine National Police earlier said that it is monitoring a low-level threat to the upcoming summit. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Why Albayanos turn to Nuestra Señora de Salvación in times of crisis
articles.summary: Even after devastating calamities and severe sickness, devotees keep their faith in Ina, seeing her as their ultimate safe haven and hope

blocks.text: ALBAY, Philippines – For centuries, pilgrims from across Bicol have journeyed to the coastal shrine of Nuestra Señora de Salvación in the small town of Joroan, Tiwi, seeking the intercession of Albay’s heavenly patroness.
Devotees believe that through their enduring faith, the Virgin Mary will answer their prayers and offer the same gift of redemption granted to all humanity.

“When pilgrims come, they come tired and scared. Yet when they find a home in our shrines, they go home refreshed and renewed,” said Reverend Father Joseph Salando, the parish priest of Joroan Church.

Sena Azores, a resident of Barangay Buyuan in Legazpi City, said that like her, most villagers living in communities near the Mayon Volcano have maintained deep devotions due to the constant dangers their communities face. They believe the patroness will protect them just as she has protected her devotees since the 1770s.
“An Inang Mapag-ampon is our best hope for salvation and protector, especially during calamities when we have done everything we can and have nothing else to rely on,” she said.
“While we prepare and follow safety advisories, our prayers to Ina give us peace of mind that we will survive any eruption or storm.”
Azores said that they always pray to the patroness to keep their families safe, especially when their children are away from home.

blocks.caption: SACRED PLEA. A devotee offers a prayer for the intercession of Our Lady of Salvation. Photo courtesy of the Joroan Church

blocks.text: With Mayon’s renewed threat of a stronger eruption following its unrest on Friday, October 30, the Diocese of Legazpi reminded residents that while they trust in the Lady through enduring faith, it is also their responsibility to remain vigilant and heed authorities’ advisories to stay safe.

“As Mayon Volcano shows signs of unrest, we entrust to the maternal care of Nuestra Señora de Salvación, Heavenly Queen of Albay, all our brothers and sisters, especially those living in communities near the volcano,” the Diocese said.
“We pray for their safety and protection, for the vigilance and wisdom of our authorities and disaster response personnel, and for the strength of families who may be affected by volcanic activity.”

blocks.caption: PIOUS OFFERING. Jimmy (right), a devotee with a disability from Harong kan Sagrada Familia, carries the crown bestowed upon Our Lady of Salvation during her pontifical coronation, while Liezl (left), an indigenous student from Joroan Elementary School, carries the crown for the Infant Jesus. Phot…

blocks.text: Beyond keeping residents safe from calamities, devotees also pray to the patroness for healing from chronic illnesses.
Bicolana visual artist Deejai Tanji, who used to visit Joroan only to see her grandparents and relatives, shared how her devotion began when both she and her partner were diagnosed with cancer.

“Life led us through broken roads, hospital visits, and moments of fear and uncertainty. Somewhere along those difficult roads, we found ourselves turning to Ina — not just to ask for healing, but to find strength in the face of things we could no longer control,” Tanji said.
She shared that knowing of the Lady of Salvation is far different from truly experiencing Her presence, especially when carrying burdens one never imagined having to bear.
“I came to Her asking for healing for someone I love, but in the process, my own faith was transformed,” she added.
“Faith gives us something invaluable: a place to find grounding, hope, and a sense of belonging.”

blocks.caption: RAINY VENERATION. Visual artist Deejai Tanji and fellow devotees gather outside the Joroan Shrine for the unveiling of the mural dedicated to Our Lady of Salvation. Photo courtesy of Deejai Tanji

blocks.text: Grateful for the strength and guidance that sustained her during her battle with cancer — which both she and her partner ultimately survived — Tanji has dedicated her art to the Lady of Salvation. She created a life-sized mural outside the shrine, where visiting devotees frequently take souvenir photos.

“I’ve learned that being a devotee isn’t just about asking for blessings, but about becoming a blessing to others. Through my art and the small ways I help my community, I try to turn what I believe into something people can actually feel and experience,” she said.

The artist hopes the younger generation of Albay residents will also discover a deep faith in the province’s heavenly mother. She emphasized that devotion to the patroness remains one of the cornerstones of Albay’s Catholic identity and its faith in Jesus Christ.

His Eminence Luis Antonio Cardinal Tagle, the dean of the college of cardinals of the Roman Catholic Church, also reminded devotees of the importance of truly knowing and drawing close to Nuestra Señora de Salvación during the Jubilee Mass commemorating the 75th anniversary of the Canonical Erection of the Diocese of Legazpi and the pontifical coronation of the image.
Tagle noted that through devotion to the patroness, the faithful can grow closer to Christ and deepen their trust in God’s enduring love.
“When you feel like drifting away from Jesus, reach out to the hand of Our Lady of Salvation. Her hands are always outstretched to catch us and bring us closer to Him,” Tagle said.

blocks.caption: HOLY CORONATION. Legazpi Bishop Joel Baylon crowns the Infant Jesus during the pontifical coronation of Our Lady of Salvation on October 28, 2026. Photo courtesy of Albay Cathedral

blocks.text: For the people of Albay, turning to Ina in times of crisis is an impulse forged over centuries: long before today’s fears of volcanic eruptions and severe typhoons, the sanctuary at Joroan was born out of centuries of vulnerability to violent storms and raiders.

In 1770, Don Silverio Arcilla, a haciendero (estate owner) from Cagnipa (now Joroan), was alerted by his tenant, Mariano Dacuba, about a chopped calpe tree trunk that did not wilt after being severed from its base. Seeking guidance, Arcilla consulted the parish friar of Buhi.

The friar commissioned a sculptor named Bagacumba to carve sacred images from the trunk. Bagacumba carved three images from the wood: Nuestra Señora de Salvación, San Antonio de Padua, and Nuestra Señora de la Soledad.

According to historical records, the image of Our Lady of Salvation was first lent to Cagnipa on August 25, 1776, on the condition that residents build a chapel for the image. This event laid the foundation for the region’s deep devotion to the patroness.

Years later, the settlement was renamed Horoan — after a species of fish commonly caught by local fishermen —and eventually became known as Joroan. Around the same time, Tiwi separated from Malinao, and Joroan later became part of Tiwi.

blocks.caption: LITURGICAL OFFERING. A priest offers incense and prayers during a Mass outside the Shrine of Our Lady of Salvation. Photo courtesy of Joroan Church

blocks.text: Around 1805, a severe storm heavily damaged the chapel housing the image, prompting its relocation to the town center and causing devotion across Tiwi to flourish. During this period, Moro raiders frequently targeted coastal villages across Albay, but local tradition holds that through the residents’ steadfast faith, invaders repeatedly failed to set fire to houses in Joroan and Tiwi — a protection attributed directly to the patroness.

As time passed, disputes over custodianship of the image arose between devotees in Joroan and Tiwi. In 1918, an assembly representing both communities agreed to return the image to Joroan and establish Joroan as an independent parish.

On September 15, 1919, a new shrine was completed on a 16-hectare land in Joroan, paving the way for the image’s return that same year. Meanwhile, a replica of the image was enshrined in Tiwi through the efforts of Bishop John Bernard McGinley.

The Diocese of Legazpi declared Our Lady of Salvation as the Heavenly Patroness of Albay on December 8, 1975. Pope Paul VI issued a decree on February 7, 1977, granting the request of the faithful to canonically crown Nuestra Señora de Salvación of Joroan.
The diocesan coronation had previously taken place on August 25, 1976, presided over by Archbishop Jaime Cardinal Sin of Manila as “a treasured expression of our people’s faith and Marian devotion.”
The church later clarified that the first crowning was considered a diocesan coronation, not a pontifical coronation.

A second major crowning took place in 2001, presided over by Bishop Jose Sorra. This silver jubilee re-crowning commemorated the patronage and episcopal coronation with a solemn renewal of consecration.

blocks.caption: DEVOUT GATHERING. More than 6,000 devotees gather at St. Gregory the Great Cathedral in Legazpi City for the pontifical coronation of Our Lady of Salvación. Photo courtesy of The Albay Cathedral

blocks.text: On October 28, 2026, Cardinal Tagle led the pontifical coronation following a papal decree of Pope Leo XIV recognizing centuries of documented miracles and devotion to Our Lady of Salvation in the Bicol region — elevating local veneration to global papal recognition.
The diocese explained that the crowning signifies a unity of the faithful in honoring Nuestra Señora de Salvación.

“May the crown offered to Inaexpress our enduring love for the Mother of the Lord, our thanksgiving to God, and our renewed commitment to His Word, the sacraments, and service to those most in need,” the diocese stated.

Beyond ecclesiastical recognition, residents like Azores and Tanji view the coronation as a reflection of their deep love and faith in the patroness they affectionately call Ina — the heavenly mother who carries them through their greatest trials. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
articles.summary: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.

blocks.text: Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.
Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.
"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.
No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.
Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.
Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.
A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.
Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.
The president has broad discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

The election results had implied three possible options for the formation of a government: a national unity administration involving both Netanyahu and Eisenkot, a right-wing coalition involving Netanyahu and defectors from Eisenkot's bloc, or an Eisenkot-led government supported by the Arab parties.
Eisenkot and every member of his bloc bar one has previously refused to enter government with Arab parties, but there has been speculation that an agreement could be reached.
He could also attempt to reach a deal with ultra-Orthodox parties, but that too would be difficult.

There is precedent for a unity government. In 2020, following three deadlocked elections, Netanyahu and his centrist rival Benny Gantz agreed a power-sharing deal in which the leadership rotated between the two.

During his consultations with the parties, Herzog had said that to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable government, he expected "factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled".
In the period 2019 to 2022, one of the most politically fractured in Israeli politics, there were five separate elections as Netanyahu and his rivals struggled time and again to co-operate.

articles.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square
articles.summary: A gunman who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the shooter was fascinated with "radical" and "far right'…

image.caption: Krakow's 'Rynek' market square is a popular tourist destination Image: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

blocks.text: At least six people were killed and sixteen injured in a shooting on the main market square in the southern Polish city of Krakow on Saturday.
The perpetrator, a 25-year-old Polish man who acted alone, was wounded during an exchange of fire with police, authorities said.
"Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told reporters in Krakow.
"That's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow," he added.
Shooter aimed at random people, police say
The gunman aimed at random people as he drove through the city's main square, which is a popular tourist attraction.
"At around 3 pm (1400 GMT), a man who had driven into the market square in a car began shooting at random people from inside the vehicle," police said on X, adding officers were among the wounded.
Deadly shooting in popular Krakow tourist spot
"The perpetrator was shot by police ‌officers and is currently being ‌transported ​to a hospital," police said.
Later Saturday evening, Polish police chief Marek Boron said a British citizen was among those killed.
"There are six fatalities: four women and two men; three Polish women, one British national, and two people who have not yet been identified," Boron told reporters.
Krakow police had earlier said that five of the sixteen people injured in the shooting were non-Polish nationals.
Authorities later clarified that the man drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each with an automatic weapon.

blocks.caption: Police secure an area near the city's main market squareImage: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bodies found in shooter's house
On Saturday night, Tusk said that the bodies of two women and a man were found in the shooters home by police.
There was "much to suggest that they are members of the [suspect's] immediate family."
The residence is located Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.
"We have the next acts of this tragedy," Tusk told reporters.
Shooter fascinated by 'far-right' views
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said that the shooter, whom she declined to identify, was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held "ultranationalistic" and "very radical" views.
The shooter wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a long gun in the attack, said Katarzyna Cislo, a spokesperson for the Krakow police,
Numerous other weapons and ammunition were found in the gunman's car.

blocks.caption: Police personnel at the site of shootingImage: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

blocks.text: Poland to observe 2 days of mourning
Prime Minister Tusk posted to X that police were investigating the attack and called it a "tragic" incident.
Tusk later said Poland would observe two days of mourning for the victims of the shooting.
Polish President Karol Nawrocki wrote on X that his thoughts were with the victims and wounded, as well as their families.
'Poland does not stand alone,' European politicians show support
The European Union's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland, adding that "Poland does not stand alone."

"I am deeply saddened by the events in Krakow. My thoughts are with the victims and their families," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote on X, adding that "Germany stands alongside Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times."
Krakow is located about 250 kilometers (155 miles) from Warsaw, the capital of Poland.
With a population of over 800,000, Krakow is Poland's second-largest city, as well as a popular tourist destination.
